arguments.sql_query:
WITH antichol AS (
  SELECT v.drug_concept_id FROM (VALUES (1129625),(44348871),(44345074),(777221),(918906),(710062),(719174)) v(drug_concept_id)
), sedhyp AS (
  SELECT v.drug_concept_id FROM (VALUES (791967),(723013),(744740),(781039),(836715),(757352),(720727)) v(drug_concept_id)
), candidate AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, CAST(de.drug_era_end_date AS date) AS index_date, 'anticholinergic_reduction' AS pattern
  FROM omop.drug_era de JOIN antichol a ON a.drug_concept_id=de.drug_concept_id
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM omop.drug_era nx JOIN antichol a2 ON a2.drug_concept_id=nx.drug_concept_id
    WHERE nx.person_id=de.person_id AND CAST(nx.drug_era_start_date AS date)>CAST(de.drug_era_end_date AS date)
      AND CAST(nx.drug_era_start_date AS date)<=DATEADD(day,30,CAST(de.drug_era_end_date AS date))
  )
  UNION ALL
  SELECT de.person_id, CAST(de.drug_era_end_date AS date) AS index_date, 'sedative_hypnotic_reduction' AS pattern
  FROM omop.drug_era de JOIN sedhyp s ON s.drug_concept_id=de.drug_concept_id
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM omop.drug_era nx JOIN sedhyp s2 ON s2.drug_concept_id=nx.drug_concept_id
    WHERE nx.person_id=de.person_id AND CAST(nx.drug_era_start_date AS date)>CAST(de.drug_era_end_date AS date)
      AND CAST(nx.drug_era_start_date AS date)<=DATEADD(day,30,CAST(de.drug_era_end_date AS date))
  )
), eligible AS (
  SELECT c.person_id, c.index_date, c.pattern,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.person_id, c.pattern ORDER BY c.index_date) AS rn
  FROM candidate c
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id=c.person_id
  JOIN omop.observation_period op ON op.person_id=c.person_id
    AND op.observation_period_start_date<=DATEADD(day,-365,c.index_date)
    AND op.observation_period_end_date>=DATEADD(day,90,c.index_date)
  WHERE YEAR(c.index_date)-p.year_of_birth>=65
    AND (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT de2.drug_concept_id) FROM omop.drug_era de2
         WHERE de2.person_id=c.person_id AND CAST(de2.drug_era_start_date AS date)<=c.index_date AND CAST(de2.drug_era_end_date AS date)>=DATEADD(day,-1,c.index_date)) >= 5
    AND (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT co.condition_concept_id) FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
         WHERE co.person_id=c.person_id AND co.condition_start_date BETWEEN DATEADD(day,-365,c.index_date) AND c.index_date) >= 2
), fall_desc AS (
  SELECT descendant_concept_id AS concept_id FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id=436583
  UNION SELECT 436583
), analysis AS (
  SELECT e.person_id, e.pattern, e.index_date,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM omop.observation o JOIN fall_desc f ON f.concept_id=o.observation_concept_id
      WHERE o.person_id=e.person_id AND o.observation_date>e.index_date AND o.observation_date<=DATEADD(day,90,e.index_date)
    ) OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM omop.condition_occurrence co JOIN fall_desc f ON f.concept_id=co.condition_concept_id
      WHERE co.person_id=e.person_id AND co.condition_start_date>e.index_date AND co.condition_start_date<=DATEADD(day,90,e.index_date)
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS fall90
  FROM eligible e WHERE e.rn=1
)
SELECT pattern, COUNT(*) AS n_patients, SUM(fall90) AS falls_90d, CAST(100.0*SUM(fall90)/NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS decimal(8,2)) AS fall90_percent
FROM analysis
GROUP BY pattern
ORDER BY fall90_percent ASC;

The MedCP clinical query timed out repeatedly, so I can’t honestly report a verified 90-day fall proportion from the EHR cohort.

Mechanistically, the pattern I would expect to be followed by the lower 90-day fall proportion is **deprescribing sedative-hypnotics**, especially benzodiazepines and Z-drugs, because their fall biology is more directly motor/sedation-linked:

- **Sedative-hypnotics**: enhance **GABA-A** signaling → CNS depression, slowed reaction time, impaired postural reflexes, ataxia, dizziness, somnolence, confusion.
- **Anticholinergics**: block **muscarinic acetylcholine** signaling → delirium/confusion, blurred vision, impaired attention, urinary urgency, and sometimes orthostasis; also fall-relevant, but often less directly gait-suppressing than GABAergic drugs.

The MedCP knowledge graph supported fall-relevant adverse effects for both classes, but sedative-hypnotics showed a consistent cluster of **dizziness, somnolence, confusion, hypotension/orthostasis, and ataxia** across zolpidem, benzodiazepines, and related agents.

So: **sedative-hypnotic reduction is the more biologically plausible lower-fall pattern**, but the actual EHR proportion remains unresolved because the cohort queries exceeded the backend timeout.
